title: Olivia Rodrigo Clarifies AI Stance Following 'Invasive' Tech Investor Dating Rumors: 'Absolutely No'
source_used: The Hollywood Reporter (cover interview), relayed by Billboard
key_facts: In her cover story for The Hollywood Reporter, published Wednesday 7 Oct 2026, the pop singer-songwriter Olivia Rodrigo says she would never use AI in her music.
She tells the magazine: 'Absolutely no. Hard line on that.' She says the closest she came was a joke with her producer about asking ChatGPT for a title idea.
Photos of her with a man believed to be a private equity associate for an investment firm surfaced in July; she says she is single.
She says being stalked outside her home and having those pictures used as evidence against her is 'the craziest thing'.
The article notes that AI music companies such as Suno face lawsuits and complaints from artists over unlicensed training music.
quote_evidence: “Absolutely no. Hard line on that,” she told the publication.
“I’m single, I don’t have a boyfriend,” the Grammy winner emphasized to THR
why_it_matters_hint: A major pop singer sets a firm no-AI line for music, while AI music is facing lawsuits.
notes: Read in full (Billboard, HTTP 200). Billboard relays The Hollywood Reporter cover interview, so THR is the source printed. THR's own URL is not in the text we read; the Billboard link is used and this is noted.
